findings.finding: Fresh seed 20261009 initialization equals unchanged direct model builder in the same CPU runtime. All training hyperparameters and ordered mechanics remain the archived naive pilot policy; only declared route-B identities, fixed scale offset, STE documentation and export metadata differ. Production milestones remain 50/75/90; CLI hard-stops at 5 and rejects warmstart, 100-epoch run requests and unsupported CPU/synthetic/control arguments.

E4 source codes and scales remain unchanged. E2M3 keeps sign, two highest source exponent bits and three mantissa bits, then source E8M0 code+6 after integer promotion; E2M1 is derived E2M3 code>>2 with identical E2M3 scales. No lower encoder, rounding route C, learned scales, clipping, wrapping or element-bias correction. All 254 finite source codes agree with an independent oracle and archived posthoc route B; all 249 shiftable scale codes and zero/padding cases are covered, with overflow/nonfinite guards.

Identity STE is exact with respect to G(W), without multiplying backward by 64; original G(W) derivatives remain. High/middle/low passes 8,6,4 use original hard CE then recursive detached softteachers, summed gradients and one Adam update per minibatch. A32, FP32 masters/gradients/Adam, dropout RNG sequence and normal three-bank BN learning remain unchanged. Independent manual training comparisons pass.

findings.finding: Actual main/check and create_context/dependency/codeccheck/trainingcheck/feedback path completes with PASS. Only runtime device selection and legacy Tensor.cuda calls are adapted to CPU in the test process. No real dataset was downloaded or trained.

Actual main/run loop completed five tiny epochs, 10 Adam updates and 30 training passes. Direct lower tensor and element encoders were patched to raise; all passes succeeded using the shared source chain. Source-triplet and plus6/mantissa scale audits, end-of-phase cache cleanup, teacher labels, short final batch coverage, prediction histograms, master updates, BN state and selected checkpoint metrics passed.

Both common selected checkpoints produce saved E4 sources and all six compact mode exports with matching source hashes and correct scale metadata. Frozen models reconstructed solely from saved E4 codes have exact logits matching each own-mode export while every encoder and G(W) is forbidden. FP32 MX masters are absent from compact payloads; required BN/auxiliary state remains.

Own epoch 2 checkpoint resumes through epoch 5 with exact CPU model/optimizer/scheduler/RNG agreement with continuous training, including testfixture LR transitions. Epoch-boundary stop is reported as stopped rather than completed; old naive contract and already completed pilot checkpoints are refused before restore/updates. Invalid production CLI requests create no output. Verified source files, runtime package, fixture data and input checkpoint hashes remain unchanged.

All 10 notebook cells and 6 figures execute in memory on actual continuous, early-stop and resumed runner outputs. Epoch 5/last and common E4-selected-best checkpoints, scale64 audit totals, hard/soft loss labels and synthetic diagnostic outcomes are handled correctly; no epoch 100 accuracy is claimed. limitations: No genuine SVHN accuracy or real GPU training/timing was measured here.
Windows PowerShell commands and CUDA runtime still require the user local check; exact epoch-boundary restore was verified on CPU only.
Original cudnn.benchmark backend policy remains, so bitexact CUDA resume is not promised.
FP32 convolution with emulated MX weights is retained; no native low-bit throughput claim.
Five-epoch software validation does not predict 100-epoch accuracy or validate scientific improvement.
